verdicts.title: The photometry 'Uncertainty' column mixes two units: magnitudes for target/check rows and raw ADU flux noise for every comparison-star row, ~3 million times larger
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently. Source at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/science_processing_service/private_helpers.dart:465-471 is exactly as cited: uncertainty: drift.Value<double?>(checkUncertainty ?? star.flux / (star.snr.isFinite ? star.snr.clamp(1.0,1e6).toDouble() : 1.0)). checkUncertainty is only non-null on the isCheck branch, where it is 1.0857*sqrt(variance) -- a magnitude sigma (lines 442-450). Every comparison row therefore falls through to flux/SNR, which is ADU flux noise. Verified in the scratch DB: select role,count(*),min(uncertainty),max(uncertainty),max(abs(uncertainty-flux/snr)) group by role -> check|99|5.6e-4|7.1e-4|2354.4, comparison|297|1912.68|2211.76|0.0 (exact identity, not approximate), target|99|5.4e-4|6.8e-4. Verified in the exported CSV /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv: header is 'Session ID,Image ID,Object ID,Role,X,Y,Flux,Differential Magnitude,SNR,Uncertainty,Is Outlier,Timestamp' and column 10 is 6e-4 for target/check and ~2e3 for comparison. One column, two physical quantities, no unit column. file:line is correct.

verdicts.title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude, so a self-discovered transient is announced as 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE'
verdicts.reasoning: Code and data both check out. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 is exactly `final magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs();` and is passed straight into TransientAlert.magnitude (the apparent-magnitude field consumed by every alert surface). packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/widgets/transient_card.dart:580-588 _getBrightnessInfo buckets magnitude<=6 NAKED EYE / <=10 BINOCULAR / <=14 SMALL SCOPE, called at :532 and rendered as 'mag ${magnitude.toStringAsFixed(1)}' at :553. DB: transient_detections has exactly one row, kind=newSource delta_mag=-2.35 snr=18.4, and the table has no apparent-magnitude column at all, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction. Because a difference-image delta magnitude larger than ~6 is essentially impossible, every First Light self-discovery with a measured delta is bucketed NAKED EYE or BINOCULAR. Cited file:line is precise (mapper :20, card :553 and :580-588). Also confirmed live on my own profile: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed — possible new transient / mag 2.4 / NAKED EYE' for the row whose delta_mag is -2.35.

verdicts.title: Stack & Share byte-swaps every pixel when 'Apply calibration' is on (the default), so it reports 'Reference frame has only 0 stars' and cannot stack anything
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced live on my own profile (:82, v-science-review) against session 3 (M51, 8 x 300s L, BITPIX=16 BZERO=32768). Stack & Share opens with 'Apply calibration' ON; pressing Start with untouched defaults gives 'Stack & Share failed / SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment)' and the log shows 'Reading FITS linear data: .../audit_L_024.fits' x2 then 'Starting live stacking from data: 512x512 (262144 pixels)'. Flipping ONLY the 'Apply calibration' toggle off and pressing Start on the same 8 frames gives 'Starting live stacking with reference: .../audit_L_024.fits' then 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars'. Root cause verified in source and it is exactly as stated: native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/fits.rs:322-365 encodes the ImageData buffer with to_le_bytes for BITPIX 16/32/-32/-64, while native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:1530-1561 image_data_to_linear_f64 decodes U16/U32/F32/F64 with from_be_bytes. Arithmetic matches the observed symptom: background 440 ADU = 0x01B8 stored LE as [B8,01] and read BE as 0xB801 = 47105; a 40614 ADU star = 0x9EA6 -> [A6,9E] -> 0xA69E = 42654, i.e. stars go DARKER than the swapped background, which is why the detector finds 0. Independent pixel check of audit_L_024.fits: median 420, MAD-sigma 22.2, 40 peaks, max 40916. Cited file:line is right, with one correction worth passing to the fixer: the finding says the bug is reached from stack_and_share_service.dart:724 _loadRawU16 -> apiReadFitsLinearData, which is correct, but image_data_to_linear_f64 has a SECOND caller, api_compute_fits_quality_maps at imaging.rs:2235, so the same byte-swap corrupts the FITS quality-map endpoint too. Blast radius is wider than the finding states.

verdicts.title: A single sub that fails alignment aborts the entire Stack & Share run and deletes the partial result, even though the code counts 'rejected' frames as a normal outcome
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced live, twice. With 'Apply calibration' off on the 8-sub session: 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_017.fits' / 'Frame 2 stacked (2 total, 0 rejected)' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_018.fits' / 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' / 'Live stacker stopped and resources released' 1 ms later. Frames 019-024 were never attempted, the dialog read 'Stack & Share failed - SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Alignment residual too high: 10.34px (max 10.00px))', and sqlite3 'select id,session_id,frames_stacked from stacked_results' was unchanged (3 pre-existing rows) before and after both runs. Code confirms the mechanism and the cited lines are exact: stack_and_share_service.dart:328 is literally `final result = await _addStackFrame(` inside `for (final frame in followers)` with no try/catch, and :335-340 is the framesRejected accounting (`if (stackedCount <= lastStackedCount) framesRejected++;`). That counter is genuinely unreachable: every rejection path in native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs (too few stars :447, too few matches :471, residual too high :495) returns Err, and the only Ok path accumulates and increments the stacked count, so add_frame can never return Ok with an unchanged count. One location nit: the finding cites ':484' for the run-level catch that deletes the row; in the current file the catch is at :486 and the deleteResult call is at :493.
verdicts.corrected_severity: P1 is defensible but P0 is arguable: combined with the 10.34px registration finding, one rejected sub is guaranteed on real dithered data, so this reliably destroys the entire run's output.

verdicts.title: Registration reports a 10.34px alignment residual for a pure 2.2px translation of the same 40-star field, so even the working path cannot stack; match_radius_px defaults to 50px
verdicts.corrected_severity: P1 (correct, but treat as P0 in combination with the Stack & Share abort finding -- together they make the feature unable to finish a run)
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced live and deterministically: two consecutive Stack & Share runs on the same 8 subs both logged 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' for audit_L_018.fits against reference audit_L_024.fits, to the same 0.01 px. I measured the true geometry independently with my own FITS reader + peak finder + nearest-neighbour match (no app code): both frames contain 40 stars, every star pairs at 2.21-2.25 px, and the offset is a pure translation dx = -1.001, dy = +1.999 with per-star scatter of 0.008/0.006 px -- i.e. a rigid fit on correct pairs gives an essentially zero residual, so 10.34 px is ~5x wrong, not a marginal call. Config defaults cited are exact (stacking.rs:91 match_radius_px 50.0, :92 match_flux_tolerance 0.7, :94 max_alignment_residual_px 10.0) and so are the fit/residual sites (:485 compute_affine_transform, :487 compute_alignment_residual). CAVEATS a fixer must not skip: (a) I verified the transform math itself is self-consistent -- compute_affine_transform is a standard Procrustes rigid fit and AffineTransform::apply at :272-276 applies exactly that transform, so the inflated residual cannot come from a fit/apply mismatch; the remaining explanation is bad correspondences, which supports but does not prove the finding's 50 px-radius story. (b) The finding's headline 'even the working path cannot stack' is too strong: in the same run audit_L_017.fits (offset dx -2.0, dy -1.0) aligned and stacked fine, so the failure is per-frame, not total. (c) The real fix is almost certainly a robust fit (outlier rejection / RANSAC over the matched pairs), not just a smaller match_radius_px -- tightening the radius alone would relocate the defect rather than remove it. ONE MORE ALTERNATIVE CAUSE the fixer must exclude before touching match_radius_px: the inflated residual could equally come from bad CENTROIDS out of detect_stars (the reference frame here contains a near-saturated star, and the same detector returns 0 stars on audit_L_001.fits which my own peak finder reads as 40 clean stars -- see the 'Integrate now' finding). Wrong centroids and wrong correspondences produce the identical observable. Note also that the post-session integration path (registration.rs) reports 0.11 px residual on comparable frames, so the defect is specific to the live-stacker registration in stacking.rs.
verdicts.duplicate_of: Not a duplicate, but shares a root theme with the 'Integrate now' P0: in both, the app's star detector fails on a reference frame that demonstrably contains 40 clean stars, and nothing downstream rejects or re-chooses that reference.

verdicts.title: 'Integrate now' silently threw away 8 of 9 subs and presented the 1-frame result as a finished master, with no error, warning or count anywhere in the UI
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on my own profile. I first restored session 1 to the finding's exact state (9 accepted, 1 rejected -- header read '9 accepted \u00b7 1 rejected', panel read 'Will integrate 9 accepted subs using Winsorized sigma'), then pressed Integrate now. Result: a new master (id 14) with stats_json {"framesIntegrated":1,"framesRejected":8,"rmsResidual":0.0,"totalIntegrationSec":300.0} and 8 integrated_master_frames rows reading 'registration failed: too few stars to register: reference=0, frame=4|11|29|30, need >= 3'. The UI after the run: the Masters card reads 'M51 \u00b7 L / 1 frame \u00b7 00:05:00 integration \u00b7 L', the header still reads '9 accepted \u00b7 1 rejected', and the whole accessibility tree contains no error, warning, or rejected-count node for that run -- 89% of the night vanished with zero feedback. Both halves of the finding hold and the cause is nailed down further than the finding states: the reference is a frame the app's own detector scores 0 stars on (audit_L_001.fits, the sub with the brightest, near-saturated star at 57952 ADU); my independent peak finder sees 40 well-separated stars in it, and with that sub culled the same button integrates 7 of 7 at 0.11 px residual, so the reference choice is the whole defect. On the reporting half, the cited locations are right and I can name the exact gap: session_review_controller.dart:710 integrate() is exact, workbench_view.dart:190 `final outcome = state.lastOutcome` is exact and is consumed only at :193 for previewPath; MasterPreviewView.fromOutcome (master_preview_view.dart:33-42) is the ONLY widget that renders '${r.framesIntegrated} frames \u00b7 ${r.framesRejected} rejected' and its sole caller is ab_compare_panel.dart:284, while the workbench master card at workbench_view.dart:353 uses MasterPreviewView.fromMaster, whose stat line has no rejected term at all.
verdicts.duplicate_of: Not a duplicate. Shares a root theme with the 10.34px registration finding (star detection failing on a reference frame that contains 40 clean stars), but this is the post-session integration path and that one is the live stacker.

verdicts.title: Project-growth panel groups subs by UTC calendar day, so one continuous evening is reported as two nights and every night is dated a day late
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced verbatim in the running app. Session Review > Narrative > 'This project over time' renders '2.0h integrated \u00b7 24 frames across 4 nights', 'Best night: Jul 28 \u00b7 0.5h', axis Jul 26 / Jul 28 / Jul 29 / Jul 30 -- character-for-character the finding's evidence. Ground truth from the DB: three observing sessions (Audit Night A 2026-07-25 21:00, B 2026-07-27 21:00, C 2026-07-29 19:30 local America/New_York), and master 1's 24 accepted subs group as 2026-07-26|10, 2026-07-28|6, 2026-07-29|4, 2026-07-30|4 by UTC day but 2026-07-25|10, 2026-07-27|6, 2026-07-29|8 by local day. Audit Night C is one continuous 19:30-20:20 local run, and 20:00 EDT is exactly 00:00 UTC, so it is cut in half. I also saw the day-late half in isolation earlier in the same session: with a single-night master the panel read '1 frame across 1 night' and labelled it 'Jul 26' for a session whose header reads '2026-07-25 21:00'. Cited location is exact: smart_project_service.dart:679 `static DateTime _dayOf(int epochSeconds)` returns DateTime.utc(dt.year, dt.month, dt.day); its one call site is :583 inside _foldedSubs (captureDate), which feeds growthCurve (:279-287) and _meanWeightByNight (:606-607) behind bestNight (:318). The finding also names reReferenceAdvice (:341) -- that one shares _foldedSubs but I did not verify it consumes captureDate, so treat that third consumer as unconfirmed.

verdicts.title: Narrowband mixer 'Apply palette' is a dead control: no composite, no file, no error, no log line
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with a control experiment that rules out the obvious false-positive explanations. Four presses of 'Apply palette' (two before and two after re-measuring the button position from a fresh screenshot, the last one clicked dead-centre on the button) produced: narrowband_composites still 0 rows, no new .fits under the masters output dir, no error/composite node in the accessibility tree on six consecutive polls, no toast in a screenshot taken 1.0 s after the click, and nothing in the app log. The click mapping is proven good: a click 120 px below the same button, on 'Run both' in the A/B panel, fired immediately and produced 15+ native '[STAR_DETECT] Image 512x512 ... Detected 29 stars' lines plus a visible 'Preview... 100%' progress bar. Preconditions are satisfied -- three finalized masters (Ha 20 / OIII 15 / SII 10) with on-disk master_fits_path files, so runNarrowband's `inputs.length < 2` early-out cannot fire, and NarrowbandChannelRef.fitsPath is populated straight from m.masterFitsPath (controller :366-370). The cited chain (narrowband_mixer_panel.dart onApply -> workbench_view.dart:304 -> session_review_controller.dart runNarrowband -> post_session_seam combineChannels) matches the source, with small line drift: workbench_view.dart:304 is exact, runNarrowband is declared at :1233, and combineChannels is at post_session_seam.dart:326-333 (the finding says :327). ONE CAVEAT for the fixer: I could not pin which link is broken. Two candidates fit every observation equally -- the button's onPressed never invoking onApply, OR bridge.apiCombineChannels never returning (which would be invisible because SkotiqButton here is constructed without isLoading, so `combiningNarrowband: true` produces no spinner). Dart-side logging does not reach app.log in this build, so log silence alone does not discriminate. Do not fix one link on faith.

verdicts.title: First Light's 'Could not load candidates' Retry button does not re-query -- the error survives Retry and a tab round-trip, and only a full app restart clears it
verdicts.location_wrong: The Retry action is NOT missing an invalidate. first_light_view.dart:406-410 already reads onPressed: () => ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider). The provider being invalidated lives in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_detections_provider.dart:138-152 -- a StreamProvider returning transientDetectionsDaoProvider.watchRecentDetections(...), i.e. a cached Drift query stream. A fixer sent to first_light_view.dart will find a correct-looking Retry and may wrongly close this as a false positive; the broken link is that invalidating the provider does not produce a fresh execution of the underlying Drift stream.
verdicts.reasoning: Symptom reproduced exactly, step for step. I set transient_detections.tile_id to the TEXT value 'tile-042' (SQLite affinity allows it), restarted, and Analytics > Science > First Light rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-042' with a Retry button. I then fixed the row from outside the app (update ... set tile_id=261982; typeof now 'integer'), pressed Retry twice, and switched to the Science sub-tab and back: identical error text including the stale 'tile-042' fragment on every check. Killing and restarting the app made the same tab render 'Possible unknown transient / 13h 29m 52.7s +47 11' 43.1"'. TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) See location_wrong: Retry does call ref.invalidate, so the finding's framing 'Retry must invalidate the provider' is already satisfied in source -- the defect is downstream of the invalidate. (2) The finding's SECOND claim -- that editing a row outside the app and switching tabs still showed the old value, therefore 'the candidate list is fetched once per app launch and is never refetched' -- does not follow and I am not confirming it. The provider is a Drift watch stream, and Drift's stream store cannot observe writes made by a different process on the same file, so an external sqlite3 edit going unnoticed proves nothing about whether new in-app detections push through. That sub-claim needs a re-test with an in-app write before anyone acts on it. Severity: the dead Retry is real, but the only demonstrated route into the error state is a value the app itself never writes, so user-facing frequency is low -- P2 fits better than P1.
